title.value: An act to add Chapter 13.5 (commencing with Section 108970) to Part 3 of Division 104 of the Health and Safety Code, relating to public health.
title.provenance:
CHAPTER 762
An act to add Chapter 13.5 (commencing with Section 108970) to Part 3 of Division 104 of the Health and Safety Code, relating to public health.

location.provenance: The people of the State of California do enact as follows:

reference.provenance: AB  1817,  Ting.  Product  safety:  textile  articles:  perfluoroalkyl  and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS).

status.provenance: [Approved by Governor September 29, 2022. Filed with Secretary of State September 29, 2022.]

date.provenance: [Approved by Governor September 29, 2022. Filed with Secretary of State September 29, 2022.]

pfas_definition.provenance: 'Perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances' or 'PFAS' means a  class  of  fluorinated  organic  chemicals  containing  at  least  one  fully fluorinated carbon atom.

type.provenance: This bill would prohibit, beginning January 1, 2025, any person from manufacturing, distributing, selling, or offering for sale in the state any new, not previously owned, textile articles that contain regulated PFAS.

date.provenance: This bill would prohibit, beginning January 1, 2025, any person from manufacturing, distributing, selling, or offering for sale in the state any new, not previously owned, textile articles that contain regulated PFAS.

who.provenance: This bill would prohibit, beginning January 1, 2025, any person from manufacturing, distributing, selling, or offering for sale in the state any new, not previously owned, textile articles that contain regulated PFAS.

products.provenance: This bill would prohibit, beginning January 1, 2025, any person from manufacturing, distributing, selling, or offering for sale in the state any new, not previously owned, textile articles that contain regulated PFAS.

value: outdoor apparel for severe wet conditions until January 1, 2028
exceptions.provenance: Paragraph  (1)  does  not  apply  to  outdoor  apparel  for  severe  wet conditions until January 1, 2028.

intentionally_added.provenance: PFAS that a manufacturer has intentionally added to a product and that have a functional or technical effect in the product

type.provenance: The bill would require a manufacturer of a textile article to provide persons that offer the product for sale or distribution in the state with a certificate of compliance stating that the textile article is in compliance with these provisions and does not contain any regulated PFAS.
